answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a VDF’s continuous sequence of modular squarings before producing a Wesolowski proof. The squarings in one chain depend on the previous result, so GPUs cannot parallelize that chain to remove its elapsed-time cost. An attacker may run separate clones concurrently, but each still faces the sequential delay. Domain-separated inputs such as sonnet, saffron, and opal prevent proofs from being reused across identities.
